description: This record is a set of case studies of low temperature district heating (LTDH) systems published on 4 June 2020 in the Celsius Toolkit on the European Commission's Smart Cities Marketplace. It describes examples from around the world, with results in the form of measured data and lessons learned where available, and states that it is mainly a literature review of projects that have been studied academically or in other contexts and is not exhaustive. For each case the main data are supply and return temperatures, design and, where possible, measured values, the design temperatures for space heating and domestic hot water, and the technologies used to reach these levels, with references for contacts. The page opens with Albertslund, Denmark, where about 2,200 social housing dwellings from the 1960s were renovated to low-energy standards between 2011 and 2015 with solar panels and a new low-temperature network, and continues with further cases not read here. Coverage is mainly European. Access: web page, free; no licence is stated. Caveats: data quality varies by case and some cases carry little data. It suits design and retrofit planning of heat networks, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
